# 1 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_007_page_001.jpg

---

1. In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius son of Seleucus broke out of Rome with a small escort, landed at a city on the coast, and seized the throne.
2. As he was moving into the royal palace, the troops rounded up Antiochus and Lysias and brought them to him.
3. When he heard about it he said: "Don't bring them in front of me."
4. The soldiers killed them. Demetrius sat down on the throne.
5. Israel's lawless men, every last ungodly one of them, made straight for him. Leading the pack was Alcimus — who wanted the high priesthood for himself.
6. They stood before the king and accused the people: "Judas and his brothers have killed all your friends and driven us out of our own land.
7. Send someone you trust. Let him come see what Judas has done to us and to the king's territory. Punish him. Punish everyone supporting him."
8. The king chose Bacchides — one of the king's Friends, governor of the Great Plain, a powerful man and loyal — and sent him.
9. He sent Alcimus along too, confirmed his appointment as high priest, and ordered him to take revenge on Israel.
10. They moved into Judah with a large army. Bacchides sent word to Judas and his brothers with smooth, peaceful language — lies.
11. Judas and his brothers didn't buy it. They could see the size of the force.
12. A delegation of scholars came out to negotiate a settlement with Alcimus and Bacchides.
13. The Hasideans were the first Israelites to seek peace with them — they said: "A priest descended from Aaron has come with this army. He won't harm us."
14. Alcimus made his speech. He took an oath: "We have no intention of hurting you or your people."
15. They believed him. He seized sixty of them and killed them all in one day — fulfilling the scripture that says:
16. "The flesh of your faithful ones and their blood they poured out all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
17. The whole people was gripped by terror and dread. They said: "There's no truth in them, no justice. They've broken every promise they ever made."
18. Bacchides left Jerusalem and camped at Beth-zaith. He seized many of the deserters from his own side, killed them, and threw some of the people into the great cistern.
19. He handed the country over to Alcimus, left troops with him, and went back to the king.
20. Alcimus fought to hold his grip on the high priesthood.
21. Everyone who was disrupting the people rallied to him. They took control of Judah and made life brutal for Israel.
22. Judas watched what Alcimus and his people were doing to Israel — it was worse than anything the Gentiles had done.
23. He swept through the whole territory of Judea, taking revenge on the deserters, and cut off their freedom of movement.
24. When Alcimus saw that Judas and his men were getting stronger, and that he couldn't hold his own against them, he went back to the king and piled up accusations against them.
25. The king dispatched Nicanor — one of his most distinguished commanders, a man who loathed Israel — with orders to wipe out the people.
26. Nicanor arrived in Jerusalem with a large force and sent Judas and his brothers another round of false peace messages:
27. "There's no need for us to fight. Come and meet me. I'll come with just a few men. Let's talk face to face."
28. He went to Judas. They greeted each other. Everything looked peaceful — but Nicanor had men positioned to grab Judas.
29. Judas found out. Nicanor had come in bad faith. From that day on Judas refused to see him.
30. When Nicanor understood that his plan had been exposed, he moved to meet Judas in open battle near Capharsalama.
31. About five hundred of Nicanor's men fell. The survivors fled to the city of David.
32. After that, Nicanor went up to Mount Zion. Priests from the sanctuary and elders of the people came out to meet him with a peaceful greeting,
33. and to show him the burnt offering being offered for the king's welfare.
34. He laughed at them. He mocked them. He treated them with contempt. He spoke arrogantly.
35. He made an oath in fury: "If Judas and his army are not handed over to me, then when I come back safely, I will burn this house to the ground." He left in a rage.
36. The priests went back inside, stood in front of the altar and the temple, and prayed, weeping:
37. "You chose this house to bear your name — to be a house of prayer and pleading for your people.
38. Now take your revenge on this man and his army. Let them die by the sword. Remember the words he said about your sanctuary. Deal with him as he deserves."
39. Nicanor left Jerusalem and set up camp at Beth-horon. The Syrian army reinforced him there.
40. Judas took position at Adasa with three thousand men. He prayed:
41. "When the envoys of the king spoke blasphemy, your angel struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
42. Do the same today. Crush this army before us. Let everyone who's left understand what he said about your sanctuary. Judge him for his wickedness."
43. On the thirteenth day of Adar the armies came together. Nicanor's army was broken, and Nicanor himself fell first.
44. When his men saw him fall, they threw down their weapons and ran.
45. The Judeans chased them a full day — from Adasa all the way to Gazara — with the signal trumpets blowing them on.
46. Men poured out of the surrounding villages of Judea. They outflanked the fleeing enemy from both sides and drove them back into each other. Every one of them died by the sword. Not a single man escaped.
47. The Judeans stripped the field. They cut off Nicanor's head and his right arm — the arm he had raised in his arrogance — and brought them and hung them up at Jerusalem for all to see.
48. The people celebrated with joy. They kept that day as a great holiday.
49. They decreed it an annual observance: the thirteenth of Adar, every year.
50. The land of Judah rested for a little while.
